Chain = ingest well data → compute composite risk score (integrity, production, mechanical, economic) → flag the top-scoring well (typically integrity threat + steep decline/rising water cut) → diagnose root cause via tests/surveys → quantify deferred volume & HSE exposure → recommend action (shut-in/reduce drawdown + integrity remediation, or lift optimization/water shut-off), prioritized by risk-reward. A specific well ID requires the field dataset.

Every KG node carries a source_record_id because it is a provenance pointer linking the node back to the raw record it came from. This matters for citation validation because it makes every fact traceable, verifiable, and auditable: validators can confirm a cited claim actually exists in a real source, detect fabricated/orphaned nodes, resolve conflicting data, and ensure regulatory reproducibility.

Water shutoff is recommended when water diagnostics (chiefly Chan plot WOR/WOR' signatures) indicate channeling through high-permeability streaks/fractures, watered-out layers or behind-casing crossflow, mechanical leaks (casing/tubing/packer), or early water breakthrough—i.e., near-wellbore, treatable water-entry problems rather than aquifer coning.
